title: Prefetch-profiled configurator with gradual safety brake for batching/caching rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build an automated configurator that recommends batching and prefix/KV cache profiles based on observed traffic shapes and then applies them via staged deployments guarded by a 'gradual safety brake'. The safety brake is a runtime limiter + SLO-aware router that enforces latency/throughput SLOs during candidate applies and provides automated rollback on anomalies. Scope: 1) offline profiler that synthesizes per-route prefetch & batching profiles from 14 days of traces, 2) online candidate generator that proposes delta config bundles (batch size, micro-window, cache TTL, prefetch ratio), 3) staged apply pipeline (shadow -> canary -> ramp) with safety brake that monitors p50/p95/p99 token latency, request throughput, tail-token latency, error rate, and quality regression signals. Success metrics: median token cost reduction >= 12% for targeted routes without SLO breaches, zero customer-visible errors, canary rollback <= 15 minutes when an anomaly is detected. Non-goals: automated prompt rewrites, model architecture changes, long-running A/B model quality experiments (those are owned by Eval team).
comments: 2026-01-12 - Maya Chen: Initial RFC drafted; included profiler prototype results for 3 example routes (search-chat, autocomplete, embeddings-micro). Observed strong prefix reuse on search-chat leading to safe cache TTL increases.

2026-01-16 - Ravi Patel: Implemented offline profiler job. It produces per-route histograms for context length and prefix-match ratios. Early flag: some low-volume routes show highly variable tail latencies — mark those as 'no-auto' candidates.

2026-01-21 - Infra review (Amir Golwala): Advised on telemetry cardinality and suggested adding sampling keys to avoid high-cost metrics. Action: limit profiler detail to top 1k routes by QPS and add 'diagnostic' toggle.
2026-01-26 - Design review (Lina Park): UX for Console suggestions; recommended two UI surfaces: 'Suggested Optimizations' list and an 'Apply Preview' with expected cost delta and risk score.

2026-01-28 - Ravi Patel: Built safety brake operator prototype. Behavior: if p95 latency increases > 15% OR error rate delta > 0.5% vs baseline in canary window, immediately scale back candidate and trigger rollback. Configurable throttles include max RPS applied and incremental canary ramp steps.

2026-01-30 - SRE (Jordan Reyes): Stress-tested canary policy under synthetic spike patterns. Found a race where prefix cache eviction plus new batch behavior caused doubled GPU memory churn; added a short cooldown window and cache warming pre-stage.
2026-02-02 - PM feedback (Amelia Torres): Add customer impact tag and manual 'hold' checkpoint before enterprise tenant applies. Also requested notification hooks for PagerDuty and Slack on rollback.

2026-02-03 - Engineering review: Preparing PRs for offline profiler, candidate generator, and safety brake runtime hooks. Need integration plan with Router service for SLO-aware routing decisions. Next: final security review and QA runbook.

Open follow-ups: (1) formalize anomaly detection thresholds per route vs global defaults, (2) add quality checkpoint using lightweight evals on representative prompt sets, (3) instrument canary metadata for audit and postmortem analysis.
rollback_playbook: 1) Safety brake detects anomaly -> mark candidate as failed; 2) Router reverts routing to last-known-good variant and pauses ramp; 3) Trigger emergency job: restore previous batch/cache config on all affected replicas; 4) Notify on-call, open incident with 'cost-optimizer' tag; 5) Capture heap/profile traces and metrics snapshot; 6) Postmortem checklist: cause, triggers, mitigations, lessons; expected mean time-to-rollback target: 10-15 minutes.
quality_checks: Lightweight eval set executed during canary (top-50 prompts per route) measuring BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-quality proxy and generation token distributions. Failure if quality delta > 3% or novel hallucination rate increases by defined heuristics.
operator_contract: Safety brake exposes a gRPC control API: ApplyCandidate(config_id, max_ramp, sample_fraction) | MonitorCandidate(config_id) | AbortCandidate(config_id). Router subscribes to MonitorCandidate and uses its verdicts for traffic split decisions.
